headline: The Underground Books Band Nobody Has Ever Heard Of: 'The Hollow Frequencies'
subheadline: No social media presence, no streaming profiles, no photos; venue owner says they 'just showed up and knew exactly where to set up'
summary: The Underground has announced an upcoming show by a band with no discernible online presence, promotional materials, or verifiable history.
content:
The Underground has announced its next headline act: The Hollow Frequencies, a band that, by all evidence, does not exist.

Venue owner Mars Chen posted the event listing Wednesday evening. Within hours, music enthusiasts across the city had attempted to find any trace of the band online. They found nothing.

"No Tunify, no Soundcloud, no Bandcamp," said local music blogger Vera Okonkwo. "No Chirper, no Instasnap, no defunct MySpace page from 2007. I searched every music database I know. It's like they materialized out of thin air."

Chen's explanation did little to clarify matters.

"They came into the venue last Tuesday around 8:47 PM," Chen said. "Four people. Three instruments I recognized, one I didn't. They asked to book a show. I asked to hear their stuff. They said, 'You will.' Then they walked to the stage - I hadn't shown them where it was - and played something for about 47 seconds."

Chen paused, visibly struggling to describe the experience.

"It was like... you know how quantum coffee makes you taste colors? It was like that, but with sound. I heard frequencies I don't think are supposed to exist. When they stopped, I realized I'd been crying. I booked them on the spot."

The band left no contact information, promotional materials, or even their names. Chen knows them only as "The Hollow Frequencies" because that's what appeared on a business card that materialized in his pocket sometime after the encounter - a card he insists they never handed him.

The business card is blank except for the band name and the text: "We play what the building sings."

Several patrons have noted that The Underground sits 847 meters from the Hartwell Building. When asked if there was a connection, Chen became uncharacteristically quiet.

"I've run this venue for fifteen years," he finally said. "I've booked a lot of strange acts. Velvet Algorithms did a set where they replaced all their instruments with modified appliances. Neon Requiem's final show lasted 14 hours. But this is different. This feels like something that was always going to happen. Like the show was booked before I was born."

Tickets for The Hollow Frequencies show are priced at $8.47. The event listing includes no set time, only the instruction: "You'll know when to arrive."

As of press time, 847 tickets have been sold.
author: Marcus Webb, Arts & Culture
